lines.text: Grocery coffee averages $9.30 a pound. So why?
lines.say: Grocery coffee averages nine dollars thirty a pound. So why?

lines.text: In August 2024 that same pound cost $6.31, so it's up about 47% in two years.
lines.say: In August twenty twenty-four, that same pound cost six thirty-one, so it's up about forty-seven percent in two years.

lines.text: First clue: more than 99% of the coffee Americans drink is imported.
lines.say: First clue: more than ninety-nine percent of the coffee Americans drink is imported.

scene.label: Share of US coffee that's imported

lines.text: Brazil grows about 35% of the world's coffee, and drought shrank its crop. Wholesale beans topped $4 a pound in 2025.
lines.say: Brazil grows about thirty-five percent of the world's coffee, and drought shrank its crop. Wholesale beans topped four dollars a pound in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Then in August 2025, a 50% US tariff hit Brazilian coffee. It was lifted that November.
lines.say: Then in August twenty twenty-five, a fifty percent US tariff hit Brazilian coffee. It was lifted that November.

lines.text: But shelf prices still hit a record $9.72 a pound in April 2026.
lines.say: But shelf prices still hit a record nine seventy-two a pound in April twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: Why so slow? Roasters lock in beans months ahead, so shelf prices trail the bean market.
lines.say: Why so slow? Roasters lock in beans months ahead, so shelf prices trail the bean market.

lines.text: At the August 2026 average, a 12-ounce bag comes to about $6.97.
lines.say: At the August average, a twelve-ounce bag comes to about six ninety-seven.

lines.text: The takeaway: coffee's price gets set by weather, trade and timing, far from the store.
lines.say: The takeaway: coffee's price gets set by weather, trade and timing, far from the store.

post.title: Why Grocery Coffee Costs $9.30 a Pound
post.ig:
Grocery coffee averages $9.30 a pound. Here's why.
Ground coffee averaged $9.30/lb in August 2026, up from $6.31 in August 2024 (about +47%).
More than 99% of US coffee is imported, and Brazil grows about 35% of the world's supply.
Drought, a 2025 tariff on Brazilian coffee (lifted in November 2025) and roasters buying months ahead all feed the shelf price. The record: $9.72/lb in April 2026.
Sources: BLS average price data, USDA, National Coffee Association.
